bib.title: Create your first knowledge graph from ontologies (Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, ch. 3)

question: How do you build a first knowledge graph from a reference ontology (HPO) to support clinicians identifying rare diseases, and which KG technology (RDF or LPG) fits?
contributions: A CRISP-DM-based walkthrough of KG construction from the Human Phenotype Ontology and an annotation TSV
A goal-driven comparison of RDF (n-ary relations, named graphs, RDF-star) and LPG for edge metadata
Cypher and Neosemantics listings for ingestion, querying and ontology-based inference

results.claim: LPG with Cypher is chosen over RDF because it puts annotation details (source, creator, date) directly on the relationship.

results.claim: Matching five clinician-identified features, the top disease matched all five.

limits: No benchmark or evaluation; one clinical use case with no accuracy, recall or clinician study.
Table 3.2 matches on exact labels; Table 3.3 shows a subset of diseases chosen for reproducible output.
Annotation merge keys on (disease, phenotype) pair only; chapter does not discuss multiple annotations per pair.
Listing 3.18 fails if the full repository ingestion (with final cleaning) is run.
Dataset is HPO as of February 2025; later HPO versions will differ.
RDF-star performance is said to need improvement and to require engine support.
practices: Start KG construction from business and domain understanding, then data understanding, preparation and KG model creation (CRISP-DM), 3.1.
Adopt one or more ontologies as the reference schema and vocabulary, with mappings from local schemas (intro).
Choose between RDF and LPG by goal; model edge-specific provenance as LPG relationship properties (3.2.2).
Create uniqueness constraints on uri and id and indexes on id for HpoPhenotype and HpoDisease before loading (3.3.1).
Configure Neosemantics to ignore vocabulary namespaces and apply Neo4j naming (uppercase relationship types) (3.3.1).
Set relationship properties only when the source column is non-null, to avoid overwriting with nulls (3.3.2).
Add human-readable properties (aspectName, evidenceName, url) to edges and batch updates with apoc.periodic.iterate (3.3.2).
Delete ontology nodes not needed for the task as a final cleaning step (3.3.2).
Use n10s.inference.nodesInCategory with SUBCLASSOF to get implicit annotations (3.5).
